skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Toolkit for testing local web applications with Playwright. It helps agents navigate pages, verify UI behavior, capture screenshots, inspect logs, and debug frontend issues.
skill.summary: Test and debug local web applications with Playwright browser automation.
skill.author: 7Spade

security_audit.summary: The static external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and Playwright example snippets, not shell execution. The localhost URL, screenshot heading, and selector guidance are also false positives for network exfiltration, upload, and reconnaissance. A semantic concern remains because the skill says Playwright will be installed automatically if missing, which can lead agents to change the environment without explicit user approval.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before installing Playwright, browser binaries, or related packages. Document the expected commands instead of implying automatic installation.
State that screenshots are saved locally for debugging and must not be uploaded or shared unless the user asks for that action.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks miss regressions and make UI bugs hard to reproduce. This skill guides Playwright-based navigation, form testing, screenshots, console log review, and responsive checks.
actual_capabilities: Navigate local or accessible web pages with Playwright.
Click controls, follow links, and fill form fields.
Verify page titles, visible text, element presence, and URLs.
Capture screenshots for debugging failed or confusing UI states.
Collect browser console messages during a test run.
Check responsive behavior across selected viewport sizes.
limitations: Requires Node.js and a running web application or accessible URL.
Does not test native mobile applications.
Complex authentication flows may need extra setup from the user.
Framework-specific routing or hydration behavior may need custom waits.

use_cases.title: Validate a new feature flow
use_cases.description: Run browser interactions that confirm navigation, form behavior, and expected page changes after a frontend update.

use_cases.title: Reproduce a UI bug
use_cases.description: Drive the browser through reported steps, collect console logs, and capture screenshots of the failing state.

use_cases.title: Review responsive layouts
use_cases.description: Check core pages across viewport sizes and identify visible layout problems before release.

prompt_templates.title: Open a local page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check for a running app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to open my local web app, confirm the page loads, and report the title and any visible console errors.

prompt_templates.title: Test a form flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to fill the main form, submit it, and verify the expected success page or validation message appears.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a failing interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce this UI issue in the browser, capture a screenshot of the failure, and summarize console logs that may explain it.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a release path
prompt_templates.prompt: Exercise the critical user path across desktop and mobile viewports, verify expected state changes, and list risks that need follow-up.

output_examples.input: Check whether the local dashboard loads and shows the expected navigation.
output_examples.output: The dashboard loaded successfully. The navigation was visible, the page title matched expectations, and no console errors appeared.

output_examples.input: Reproduce the login validation issue and capture useful evidence.
output_examples.output: The form showed the expected validation message after an empty submit. A screenshot was saved locally, and one warning appeared in the browser console.

output_examples.input: Review the checkout flow on desktop and mobile widths.
output: Desktop checkout completed with the expected confirmation page.
Mobile layout kept primary controls visible, but the order summary wrapped awkwardly.
No blocking console errors were observed during the flow.

best_practices: Start with one clear user flow before expanding coverage.
Use stable selectors such as roles or data-testid attributes.
Capture screenshots and console logs only when they help explain a result.
anti_patterns: Do not run tests against production data without approval.
Do not rely on brittle CSS class selectors when stable selectors exist.
Do not ignore timeouts or console errors during failed interactions.

faq.question: Does this skill require Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. It is written for Playwright-based browser automation and needs Node.js support.

faq.question: Can it test a deployed site?
faq.answer: Yes, if the URL is accessible and the user allows testing that environment.

faq.question: Can it handle login flows?
faq.answer: It can test many login flows, but multi-factor authentication or third-party identity providers may need manual setup.

faq.question: Does it upload screenshots?
faq.answer: No upload behavior is described. Examples save screenshots locally for debugging.

faq.question: Can it test mobile apps?
faq.answer: No. It can emulate browser viewport sizes, but it does not test native mobile applications.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
